pr_body:
Add the necessary code to support synchronous routes. I know I have been a big advocate against this in the past because it create a _bad_ error handling pattern. However, not returning is kind of frustrating for a newbie as some eslint config instructs them to not use the `async` keyword if there is no await (sigh).

This does not cause slow downs in benchmarks.

An alternative option is throwing if a sync route is used.

Fixes #2065

issue_context.title: Support synchronous routes
comments: I have not seen this in our issues, or I just don't remember it. Is this really something a lot of people are doing?

I've seen this on gitter a few times, as well as people playing with the framework.
They don't know that `async` makes the function return a promise.

I fear this solution could result in some edge case that is difficult to predict now.
How about throwing an error in the same way we are doing if the user declares an async hook with the `next` callback in the signature?

I think there are two paths we can follow here:
- the one you have suggested, who translates to being smart and trying to understand what the user wants
- throw an error and try to educate the user about the correct use of the API (and the language).

> I've seen this on gitter a few times, as well as people playing with the framework.
They don't know that async makes the function return a promise.

I would be very careful with such conclusions as long as they can't be verified. What about a twitter pool or any other survey?

Accepting anything to respond feels handy and comfortable to me. On the other side, this can already be archived with an async function.

In the short term, I agree with @delvedor to produce a better error message. In the long term, we need to check if it's really an intuition thing or just "I have no idea at all what I'm doing here".
The `setErrorHandler` will benefit from this feature because it will always be executed regardless it is a sync or async function, it is more homogeneous
